cf.title: Match jsonpath variable names exactly when checking mutability

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Match jsonpath variable names exactly when checking mutability

verdict_reasoning: No objection at levels 1a or 1b survived. Message #1 states a wrong-results bug with a reproduction, and the fix makes jspIsMutableWalker() match names as GetJsonPathVar() does. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is fixable: a back-patch to 17 makes some existing index definitions fail at restore or pg_upgrade, and the proposal gives users no way to find them first. A committer who knows the SQL/JSON code should judge the back-patch.

brief.title: Match jsonpath variable names exactly in the mutability check
brief.problem: jspIsMutableWalker() compares a jsonpath variable with PASSING argument names only over the variable name's length, so a PASSING argument "aa" can set the datatype of $a. Since commit 0f271e8e8d9, GetJsonPathVar() needs an exact match at execution, so the two can disagree. create index can then accept an expression that depends on TimeZone and return wrong results, or reject an immutable one.
brief.proposed_design: jspIsMutableWalker() also requires equal name lengths, as GetJsonPathVar() does. The patch adds two regression tests to sqljson_queryfuncs: one where the PASSING name extends the variable name, and one where it is a prefix of it. The author asks for a back-patch to 17.
user_visible_surface: create index on a JSON_EXISTS or other SQL/JSON expression with PASSING now fails with "functions in index expression must be marked IMMUTABLE" in the reported case.
Some index expressions that were wrongly rejected as mutable are now accepted.
Restoring a dump with an index that was wrongly accepted now fails at create index.
author_claims: On master, a wrongly accepted index gives 1 row with an index scan and 0 rows with a seq scan after a TimeZone change.
The cost is one strlen() for each PASSING argument the check examines, and evaluation does not change.
make check and make installcheck pass.
The code came with SQL/JSON in 17, so the fix should be back-patched there.
REINDEX does not fix affected indexes, so users must drop them or replace them with truly immutable expressions.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review.
unclear: The patch does not say whether release notes or other user guidance will tell users how to find affected indexes.
The material does not say if other callers or walkers besides jspIsMutableWalker() use the same prefix comparison.
The material does not say whether the back-patch to 17 applies cleanly or needs changes.

objections.title: Back-patch makes existing dumps and pg_upgrade fail without a way to find them
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 17.x has a JSON_EXISTS index with PASSING names like aa and a. After a minor update, pg_restore of an older dump fails at create index. A later pg_upgrade to a new major version fails at the same index. The user finds out only when the restore or upgrade stops.
objections.argument: Message #1 and the commit message say restoring such definitions "will now fail at CREATE INDEX" and that REINDEX does not help. pg_upgrade restores index definitions through pg_dump, so it fails in the same way. Neither text offers a catalog query or release-note wording that lets a user find affected indexes before the update. A committer would likely accept the wrong-results fix but ask for this guidance before a minor-release back-patch.
objections.author_must_show: What query or release-note text will let 17.x users find affected index expressions before a minor update or a pg_upgrade?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 warns that restoring such a dump fails, but gives no query or release-note text for finding affected indexes. pg_upgrade restores the schema through the same create index, so the gap is real and a new patch version can close it.

refuted.title: pg_upgrade from 17 can fail on indexes the old check accepted
refuted.failure_scenario: A 17.x user has an index like t_idx from message #1 and runs pg_upgrade to a later major version that has the fix. The binary-upgrade schema restore runs create index, the stricter check rejects it, and pg_upgrade stops partway through. pg_upgrade --check does not warn about this beforehand.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says a restore from a dump will fail, but it says nothing about pg_upgrade, which replays the same create index during schema restore. The users who hit this are the ones who already have a wrong index on disk. The proposal also gives them no way to find such indexes before an upgrade. A query in the release notes, or a pg_upgrade check, would let them drop or rewrite these indexes first.
refuted.author_must_show: How will a 17.x user find the affected indexes before pg_upgrade or a restore fails, through a release-note query or a pg_upgrade check?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers both the minor-release restore and the pg_upgrade failure and asks for the same guidance.

refuted.title: Two separate name lookups can drift apart again
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how GetJsonPathVar() matches PASSING names, or adds a new mutability walker, and does not update jspIsMutableWalker(). The mutability check and execution disagree again, and create index accepts a TimeZone-dependent expression. Users find out only when an index scan and a seq scan return different rows.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows this bug came from that drift: commit 0f271e8e8d9 made execution use exact matching, and the walker kept its own prefix comparison. The fix aligns the two comparisons but keeps two copies of the matching rule, and nothing fails if they diverge. A shared helper for finding the PASSING argument by name would keep the rule in one place. The material does not say whether other callers use the same prefix comparison.
refuted.author_must_show: Could jspIsMutableWalker() and GetJsonPathVar() share one helper for finding a PASSING argument, and do any other callers still use the prefix comparison?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a future patch that changes one lookup and misses the other; this patch does not add the duplication, it removes the present divergence. The two lookups walk different structures at plan time and at execution, and the new tests cover both mismatch directions in the walker.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade restores index definitions with create index, which now rejects indexes the old check accepted.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Message #1 says restoring a wrongly accepted index definition from a dump now fails at create index.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author asks for a back-patch to 17, which changes what create index accepts in a minor release.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What query or release-note text will let 17.x users find affected index expressions before a minor update or a pg_upgrade?
Does any code besides jspIsMutableWalker() still compare PASSING names by prefix?
Does the patch apply to the 17 and 18 branches as it is, or do those branches need a different version?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the SQL/JSON query functions and jsonpath code would have to own it; no one has replied to message #1.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in minor releases of 17 and later: some create index statements that worked now fail, including during restore and pg_upgrade. The owner also signs for the release-note guidance.
committability.author_follow_up: The author names himself as contact and invites rework of the patch; the thread has no later message that shows follow-up.

priority.reason: The bug gives wrong results from an index, but only for SQL/JSON index expressions where one PASSING name is a prefix of another. The patch is 5.0 KB, touches one source file and one regression test, and adds no user-visible surface.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the review cannot confirm that the new comparison equals the one in GetJsonPathVar(). It also cannot confirm that no other prefix comparison remains or that the back-patch applies to 17.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonpath string method $.replace(from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, "David E(dot) Wheeler", Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a non-standard jsonpath string method, $.replace(from, to), which calls the internal implementation of the SQL replace() function on a JSON string value. The author planned more text methods, such as trim(), upper() and lower().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread does not state why the author withdrew the entry. David E. Wheeler noted that replace() is not in the SQL/JSON spec, and Andrew Dunstan objected that a future spec version could add an incompatible method with the same name, so he wanted non-spec method names prefixed or capitalized. Peter Eisentraut asked for a general way to call any suitable pg_proc function from jsonpath, and the author then began sketching that design instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The thing that bothers me about the original proposal
is this: what if we add a new non-spec jsonpath method and then a new
version of the spec adds a method with the same name, but not compatible
with our method?

precedents_retrieved.title: Make selectivity example match wording
precedents_retrieved.summary: The doc patch changes the unique, non-null join selectivity example so that it divides by the maximum of the two row counts, as the prose describes, and uses num_rows in place of num_distinct. A v2 patch also rewrote the explanation of the formula in the docs and in the code comments, including the proof in the comments.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The reviewer called the smaller change valuable and was "good" apart from one wording suggestion. The thread then has no further messages before the entry was returned with feedback in November.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checks on search_path for IMMUTABLE and SECURITY DEFINER functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Greg Stark proposed checks at function creation that warn or error when an IMMUTABLE or SECURITY DEFINER function has no search_path set, so that pg_restore failures and index corruption caused by search_path dependence are avoided. A later version instead filled in search_path in proconfig for the user, and he also floated a LEXICAL option modelled on SQL-standard function bodies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed a work in progress: it failed the regression tests, and the author raised open issues himself, namely cache flushes from a per-function search_path and the loss of inlining for functions with proconfig set. Andres Freund noted in October that it did not pass tests and asked whether the author planned further work and whether the entry wanted review. No reply from the author is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This currently obviously doesn't pass tests - are you planning to work on this
further?  As is I'm not really clear what the CF entry is for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Permute underscore separated components of columns before fuzzy matching
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the fuzzy column-name matching behind the "Perhaps you meant" hint so that it also checks permutations of up to three underscore-separated words. A swap of two words costs the same as one mistyped character, and the permutation is skipped when the typed name has more than six underscores.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds opaque, almost undocumented code to the matching function, and he doubted that many users want this behavior. He also noted that adjacent underscores and leading or trailing underscores are not handled well. The visible messages show no reply from the author after this review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, we *do*
need to be concerned about its maintainability, and I think the patch
falls down badly there: it adds a chunk of very opaque and essentially
undocumented code, that people will need to reverse-engineer anytime
they are studying this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL/JSON: JSON_TABLE
precedents_retrieved.authors: Fedor Sigaev (sigaev), Alexander Korotkov (smagen), Nikita Glukhov (n.glukhov), Oleg Bartunov (oleg)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the SQL-standard JSON_TABLE function, including the PLAN clause and PLAN DEFAULT clause, on top of the separate SQL/JSON functions patch set. JSON_TABLE turns a JSON document into rows and typed columns selected by jsonpath expressions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a rebase in July 2020, and the author did not post a new version within four weeks, so it was returned with feedback. Earlier, Pavel Stehule had marked it ready for committer, after his review objections had been resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Something that has not happened in four weeks, so this is marked
as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PATCH v1] psql: Do not complete HEADER MATCH for COPY TO
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change psql tab completion so that MATCH is offered as a value of the COPY HEADER option only for COPY FROM, since the server rejects HEADER MATCH for COPY TO. The boolean values stay available in both directions, and the change covers both COPY and \copy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after Chao Li pointed out that an earlier patch already fixed the same problem. No one objected to the change itself, and the reviews called the fix correct.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The fix looks good, however, there is an earlier patch [1] already.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support multiple password-based authentication tokens concurrently
precedents_retrieved.summary: Move role passwords into a new catalog (pg_auth_password) so that a role can have several named passwords valid at the same time, each with its own expiration. Expirations are set per password through new SQL grammar or a default validity-period GUC, so that passwords can be rotated without downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The original author said he might not be able to continue the work, and Stephen Frost posted an updated version for the July commitfest while Gurjeet Singh said he planned to pick it up. No review objections or later activity appear before the entry was returned with feedback in October.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_lookup function to get all matching pg_hba.conf entries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function pg_hba_lookup that takes a database, a user and optionally an address and hostname, and returns the pg_hba.conf entries that match them, in match order. It replaces an earlier attempt at a catalog view of pg_hba.conf, which could not handle keywords in the database and user columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: At the end of the last commitfest for 9.6, Tom Lane reviewed the patch and judged it not ready to commit. He found the patch too invasive in the authentication code, raised concerns about its memory management and its function signature, and found type errors in the docs. He also doubted the use case, since a user who cannot connect cannot run the function, and suggested making log_connections record the matched pg_hba line.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And it's not very clear that it'll help
with "I can't connect", either, because if you can't connect you're
not going to be running this function.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no proposal with the same or a similar idea, and the thread does not point to an earlier discussion. The patch is a bug fix that makes jspIsMutableWalker() match GetJsonPathVar() exactly, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

The fix aligns the mutability check with the exact match GetJsonPathVar() already uses at execution. It adds no syntax, GUC, or catalog change, so the standards side is fine. The only point is how the back-patch handles existing indexes.

The patch has no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or ABI change. The only persistent effect is on indexes that already exist with definitions the fixed check would reject, and the objection above covers that.

The patch has no privilege or exposure aspect. It makes the immutability check at create index stricter and grants nothing, and a wrongly accepted index only gives wrong results on a table the creator already controls.

This is a narrow wrong-results bugfix with no hot-path cost, no new API and no extension fit question. The single objection is about preventing the same drift in the future, and a new version could address it.

This is a correctness bugfix in jspIsMutableWalker(). No existing feature, extension or setting can stop create index from accepting a TimeZone-dependent expression, so nothing from the already-exists angle applies. The fix extends the existing check and adds no second mechanism.

This is a correctness bugfix with a reproduction in message #1: an index can return 1 row while a seq scan returns 0 after a TimeZone change. Wrong results from an index need no demand evidence, and the cost of one strlen() falls only on PASSING checks.
